verdict.why:
I wrote my own classifier from the worded shape tests and did not reuse census.mjs. It ran over all 95,089 routes in stepbible_tahot_aligned_translation.jsonl.

(a) Counts. All 35 shape counts reproduce exactly. So do all 13 mark totals (123,841 occurrences altogether), the routes-per-mark figures, and the inventory's M4 row. The structural figures also match:
- route equals definition in 95,089 rows
- 46,609 keys, at most 108 routes on one key
- 0 commas, 0 parentheses, 1 semicolon
- 53,554 routes with a slash
- spanJoin joins 53,554 routes and drops an empty segment in 15

The segment evidence matches too:
- 'and' as first segment: 19,104 of 19,124 keys begin with vav; the other 20 begin with lamed
- 'the' as first segment: 2,618 of 2,619 begin with he
- 'your' as last segment: 2,364 of 2,364 have a kaf in the last three letters
- '!' as last segment: 477 of 478 keys end in he or nun
- '¿': 401 of 401 keys begin with he; 'and/ ¿': 4 of 4 begin with vav-he
- '<obj.>': 72 of 113 keys carry et/ot; 113 of 113 carry et/ot, yat or lamed
- '<prep> <the>' as first segment: 527 of 527 begin with bet, kaf or lamed
- segments never outnumber the key's letters: 53,554 of 53,554
- 3 routes are a supplied bracket alone; '[surely]' is followed by a rendering in 7 of 8

The slash spacing 63,953 'x/ y' reproduces when spacing is judged by the character next to the slash.

(b) Completeness. Every occurrence matches at least one shape. Exactly one shape each holds only with two wording fixes, listed in corrections:
- One '?' (ידעתה | do you know/ ?) matches both question.end_of_rendering and question.mark_only_segment. The draft counted it under mark_only_segment.
- hyphen.word_continued_from_before gives 70 only if 'first character of its segment' means the first non-space character. Read literally it gives 31, and 39 hyphens (e.g. 'east/ -ward') fall in no shape.

The shape tests are written in census.json, not in declaration.json, so the declaration file itself is unaffected.

(c) Falsification. No shape divides readings: divides_readings is false for all 13 marks, separates_on is null and precedence is []. So no dividing meaning can be falsified. The one candidate division is the single ';' (פלט). It is stated, counted (1) and raised as an open question.

I still probed every mark:
- Slash:
  - 5 'x/y' with no space; all are segment seams such as 'in/order that' or 'to/make', not alternatives.
  - 0 doubled adjacent segments.
  - 0 routes with more segments than key letters.
  - 20 'and/' on lamed keys and 1 'the/' on a bet key; both are stated, counted exceptions.
- Square brackets:
  - 0 '[or' alternatives.
  - 0 supplied_letters holding a whole word.
  - 66 '[the]' on keys opening with he; all are root he (e.g. היכלי | [the] palaces of), not an article in the Hebrew.
- Hyphen: 0 spaced dashes.
- '!': 6 '!' followed by English; all are 'woe! to', still one rendering.
- '?': 0 followed by English other than ' of'.
- '¿': 0 on keys not opening with he or vav-he.
- Apostrophe: all 38 are possessives (4 are "rams'"); 0 contractions or quotes.
- Colon: 0 with text after it.

Non-dividing refinements are in corrections.

(d) v3 comparison reproduces exactly, using sense-split-v1 senseSplit plus packSplit taken read-only from gloss-store-v1.mjs:
- 95,089 fields compared, 95,088 divided the same
- 1 where v3 divides and the declaration keeps whole (פלט, 'deliverance; [surely]', split by packSplit)
- 0 the other way, 0 divided differently, 0 withheld
- senseSplit alone divides 0 and marks 0 damaged; packSplit divides 1

readingOf with today's declarations-v1.json (TAHOT undeclared) gives 95,089 of 95,089 whole. With the draft merged in memory only, nothing written: 95,089 whole, 0 separated, 0 refused, 0 rows with an undeclared mark.

Files are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-mashiachsonyosef-github-io/c72302ec-11e7-5b6d-a5ab-47bb077585fe/scratchpad/punct/verify/stepbible_tahot_aligned_translation/:
- verify.mjs, which writes verify.json (run output in run.log)
- probe2.mjs, probe3.mjs and probe4.mjs, which write probe2.json, probe3.json and probe4.json
corrections: question.end_of_rendering: the worded test ('?' at the end of the route or directly before '/') also matches the lone '?' segment of ידעתה | do you know/ ?, which gives 463 matches. The stated 462 needs the test to exclude a segment that is '?' alone, or a stated precedence: mark_only_segment before end_of_rendering. This is in the census test text only.

hyphen.word_continued_from_before: 'the first character of its segment' read literally matches 31, not 70. The count reproduces as 'the first non-whitespace character of its segment' (39 hyphens follow '/ ', e.g. 'east/ -ward'). Under the literal wording those 39 fall in no shape.

Evidence 'routes_with_the_word_or: 6' (declaration '/' evidence: '6 the word or'): 12 routes carry the word 'or'. The 6 not counted are 'or?' (e.g. אם | or?, ואם | and/ or?). 6 is the count of 'or' as a whole bare segment. None of the 12 is a packed alternative: in every one 'or' is the whole rendering of או, אם or הן.

Evidence on square-bracket content ('article 7,713, be/belong 7,305, other 7,691 over all matched pairs'): the three classes sum to 22,709, but the stack-matched pairs number 22,715 (21,430 + 1,268 + 15 + 2). 22,709 is the count from a non-nesting regex, which pairs '[who/ [-ever]' as one span. be/belong 7,305 is not reproduced under an exact-form reading (6,814) or an any-word reading (7,527), and the class rule is not stated. Article 7,713 reproduces.

angle.hebrew_words 'means' lists an article held in a preposition's vowel, a preposition, or an infinitive absolute. 395 of 4,946 are none of these: subject pronouns the verb carries (<it> 90, <he> 20, <they> 17, <she> 11, <you> 5; e.g. הללה | <it> was praised) and conjunctions (<and> 32, e.g. ולתת | <and>/ to/ give; <if> 9). The general meaning (the Hebrew carries it, natural English drops it) stands. Widen the list. Does not divide.

angle.hebrew_letters 'Hebrew plural, English singular': all 884 are <s> (730) or <es> (154). 25 of them sit on keys with no yod, vav or tav, so no plural ending is visible (e.g. חלב | fat<s>, חמה | curd<s>, מצה | unleavened bread<s>, כל | baggage<s>). The plural reading is untested for these, as defective spellings or key errors. State it as unverified for those 25. Does not divide.

square.open_continues_elsewhere: 'closes in a neighboring word's route' cannot be tested from this file, which has no word positions. 2 of the 4 (האכל | [who/ [-ever] eats, and והאכל) look like a closer missing inside one word rather than a span carried to a neighbor. State it as unverified. Does not divide.
falsified_meanings: angle.hebrew_words: the listed meanings (article, preposition, infinitive absolute) miss 395 of 4,946 occurrences: verb-carried pronouns (143) and the conjunctions 'and' and 'if' (41). The broader meaning is not falsified. Does not divide.
question.end_of_rendering vs question.mark_only_segment: the two tests overlap on 1 occurrence (ידעתה | do you know/ ?). This is a defect in the test wording, not in the meaning.

examples: v3 divides where the declaration keeps whole: פלט | 'deliverance; [surely]' -> v3 ['deliverance', '[surely]'] (gloss-store packSplit at ';'); declaration ['deliverance; [surely]']
senseSplit alone (commas) divides 0 routes and marks 0 as damaged: TAHOT has 0 commas and 0 parentheses. Its only v3 division is packSplit's one ';'.
v3 withholds where the declaration prints: 0

declaration-v1.mjs readingOf: with today's declarations-v1.json (TAHOT undeclared) 95,089 of 95,089 equal the declaration. With this declaration merged in memory: 95,089 whole, 0 separated, 0 refused, 0 rows with an undeclared mark.

Page print, not division: spanJoin joins the '/' segments with ' + ' in 53,554 routes and drops an empty segment in 15 (מהזה | 'what/ /[is] this?' -> 'what + [is] this?'). This agrees with the declaration's segments_on.

questions: The one ';' (פלט, 'deliverance; [surely]'). Reading A: clause punctuation inside one reading, shipped whole, as this declaration does (1 route). Reading B: two readings, 'deliverance' and '[surely]', as today's packSplit does (1 route). In the data, all 7 other routes with '[surely]' have a rendering after it, and only 3 of 95,089 routes consist of a supplied bracket alone. One occurrence cannot establish a convention.

The '/' segments (53,554 routes, 64,013 boundaries). Reading A: one reading, printed joined with ' + ', which is what the page's spanJoin does today and what this declaration's segments_on says. Reading B: one reading whose segments also stand as separate pieces, each placed under its Hebrew segment (the RMD '+' pieces). Both are separations, not derivations, so the data cannot decide this; it is a page design ruling.

A segment that is only '!' (478 routes) or only '?' (1 route). Reading A: a sign, hidden when the signs switch is off, as '¿' (405 of 405) and a lone '<...>' (2,403 of 2,403) already are (479 routes). Reading B: text that is always drawn, as 'they lie down + !', which is what happens today because the page's signOnly regex does not list '!' or '?' (479 routes). signOnly also does not list two-bracket segments such as '[is] <to>' (131 routes) or the maqaf segment '-' (10).

Unbalanced brackets (10 routes: 4 '[' that continue into a neighboring word, 2 ']' that close a neighbor's span, 4 stray '>' in '<into> the>'). Reading A: print them as written. That is what this declaration does, and what today's engine does, since its damage rule only checks parentheses (10 routes). Reading B: hold them back as damaged, the way v3 holds back unbalanced parentheses (10 routes).
